The Universal Declaration of Human Rights ( UDHR ) is a document adopted by the United Nations General Assembly that codifies some of the rights and freedoms of all human beings . Drafted by a United Nations (UN) committee chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt , it was accepted by the General Assembly as Resolution 217 during its third session on 10 December 1948 at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris, France. [ 1 ] Of the 58 members of the UN at the time, 48 voted in favour, none against, eight abstained , and two did not vote. [ 2 ]
